svg.title: VLA model pipeline diagram
svg.desc: Editable reconstruction of a VLA model training and inference schematic. The figure contains an actions panel, next-scene multi-view image panel, central dashed VLA model frame with language model, tokenizers, instructions, ego state, aspects, command, projector, vision encoder, MovQGAN encoder/decoder, multi-view image inputs and arrows, plus right-side stage descriptions separated by a vertical divider.

g.desc: Inside the actions base frame are four small autonomous car icons progressing left to right with colored trajectory shadows and pedestrian silhouettes. Labels underneath read Safety, Progress, Comfort, and Optimal. A selection label and arrow point toward the optimal action. The layout is horizontally equipartitioned across the panel.

The top next-scene base frame holds six rounded blue-outlined image placeholders evenly spaced from left to right: front, front left, front right, back, back right, back left. The section is symmetric across a horizontal row.

The central dashed VLA model frame contains text detokenization above a language model, token streams feeding and exiting the model, a MovQGAN decoder leading upward to next-scene images, a lower instruction/state/aspect/command panel feeding through a text tokenizer, a vision encoder and projector on the right fed by lower multi-view images, and a MovQGAN encoder in the lower center. Arrows are mostly vertical and horizontal orthogonal connectors, with symmetry organized around the large language-model band.

The bottom multi-view image frame contains the current six camera-view image boxes, equally spaced, with a label below. A vertical arrow rises from the strip to the vision encoder and another arrow rises to the MovQGAN encoder.

The right side separated by a vertical gray line lists training stages. Stage 1 supervise-fine tuning uses Nuscences: 1M Images. Stage 2 instruction-tuning uses Nuscences multi-view images plus 300K QAs. These blocks are vertically arranged and centered in the right panel.
